provenance.derivation: Composed in the manner of kasane no irome, for winter: 3 of our own published entries read as layers from the outermost inward — 寒空 samu-zora (#A1B3C6), then 雪気 yuki-ge (#E3E7F1), then 寒星 samu-boshi (#2B3353). NOT a historical combination: no layer is asserted to reproduce a documented Heian kasane, and no value was read from any kasane table. Chosen by hand, not generated. Adjacent layers are separated by ΔE00 14.3, 65.0 under @irodora/color-difference 0.1.0 — each above the ΔE00 5 at which the product calls two items the same (FR-44), because a layering whose edges cannot be told apart is not one. Weights fall inward (1, 0.8, 0.6, 0.5) because each inner layer shows less than the one over it.
provenance.editorialNotes: A clear winter day: the cold sky (寒空) outermost, snow air (雪気) at its edge, and a night-blue lining (寒星) that makes both read as bright. All three carry the winter tag. The light middle layer is what gives a winter layering its sparkle against a dark lining. The name is ours (冬晴, "Winter Clearing"), coined as a seasonal image the way the historical names are; it is not presented as a traditional kasane name.
